assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base pair to another through engineered deaminase chemistry on DNA without double-strand cleavage. This is a clear, principled and genuinely new capability, with a defined chemical mechanism, rapid uptake across biology, and therapeutic use following. It is exactly the kind of result that opens vast, previously unforeseen possibilities, and it can be explained to a broad audience in a sentence.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group conceived and demonstrated cytosine and adenine base editing; Komor (CBE) and Gaudelli (ABE) were the lead experimentalists. A prize to Liu alone or to Liu with the two first authors is defensible. The CRISPR prize in 2020 and the separate prime-editing candidate need to be kept distinct from this discovery.
assessment.maturity: About a decade since the first report, with extensive independent replication, many derivative editors and first clinical data. Timing is good, though long-term clinical safety outcomes are still accruing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to cite base editing and prime editing together or separately.
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may make some members regard this as an engineering extension.
Long-term clinical safety and off-target (including bystander and RNA-level) effects are not fully settled from my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell brings physical-chemical concepts (thermodynamics of demixing, multivalency, material properties) to cell biology and reframes how compartments without membranes form. As a physicist I value the underlying principle and the quantitative framework, and the idea has reshaped research across cell biology, biophysics and disease.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids (2009); Rosen's multivalent signalling-protein work (2012) supplied the molecular-valency principle. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar understanding, which makes a clean three-person line contestable. I would insist the committee separate the original discovery from later refinements.
assessment.maturity: Highly active field and broadly accepted as concept, but debate continues over which in-cell assemblies are truly phase-separated condensates versus other assemblies, and in vivo relevance of some claims has been questioned. Probably still maturing but near the point of timeliness.
uncertainties: Controversy about in vivo physiological relevance and artefacts of overexpression.
Whether the prize is chemistry or physiology/medicine in character.
Credit allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules by electrical current blockade in a nanopore is a nanophysics-meets-chemistry concept that I find compelling: single-molecule electrical detection, with protein-engineered pores and motor-enzyme-controlled translocation, yielding long-read sequencing devices that are now commercial and widely used. It delivers a clear new capability with quantitative performance.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon and Deamer's 1996 alpha-hemolysin demonstration, Branton and Deamer's early sequencing concept, Bayley's engineered pores and Akeson's enzyme-ratcheted single-nucleotide-resolution reading are all decisive; the credit is spread across more than three people and I would need to understand sequence of ideas carefully. I recall that Branton has died, which would limit the options, but I have not verified it.
assessment.maturity: Technology is more than two decades old, independently validated, and routinely used for long-read genome and RNA sequencing, so maturity is strong.
uncertainties: Credit split among five names, with possible need for a three-person compromise.
Whether it would be viewed as sequencing technology (already recognized in 1980 and 2020 contexts) rather than chemistry.
Status of Branton, and whether early conceptual claims precede experimental demonstration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure theory with dynamics through an extended Lagrangian, enabling ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and reactions for the first time. It has a clear underlying principle, and a very large lasting influence on materials science, water and condensed-phase chemistry. It is a clean, physics-grounded achievement of the sort I find easy to justify.
assessment.attribution: Two-person attribution is unambiguous: the 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello. Parrinello also appears in the metadynamics and machine-learned potential candidates, so the committee might prefer to recognise him through one coherent citation instead of several.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of validation, with the method embedded in widely used codes. It is arguably overdue, not premature, though it overlaps the 1998 and 2013 prizes in computational chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a broader computational-dynamics citation incorporating metadynamics or machine-learned potentials.
Prior computational chemistry prizes (1998, 2013) may reduce appetite for another one soon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites as solution-processable absorbers moved from a few percent to over 25 percent certified efficiency in about a decade, approaching the Shockley-Queisser limit, and have redirected photovoltaic research. The physics of defect tolerance and the combined chemical tunability give a strong principle plus a clear performance result.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park and Snaith's solid-state (2012) cells established the high-efficiency architecture, while Grätzel, Seok, and Kanatzidis made major contributions. Six credited names against a maximum of three leaves the decisive-contribution question contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies replicated across many laboratories, but operational stability, lead content and scale-up remain unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat premature from a device-maturity standpoint.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercial viability are not established.
Disputed priority among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Grätzel.
Could be seen as a physics or materials contribution rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by reversible-terminator chemistry on clustered single molecules cut the cost of genome sequencing by orders of magnitude and transformed biology and medicine. It is a clear case of chemistry (nucleotide chemistry, surface attachment, single-molecule fluorescence) enabling a transformative capability.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry, the dominant platform; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing and Mayer's work on parallel clusters are alternative strands. Selecting Balasubramanian and Klenerman is the cleanest chemistry-centred citation but it leaves out important parallel inventors.
assessment.maturity: Technology is two decades old and universally adopted, so maturity is complete. The field consolidated, which strengthens rather than weakens the case.
uncertainties: Competing technologies and priority claims (454, Lynx, Manteia/Mayer, Illumina commercial development).
Sanger and Gilbert's 1980 prize and the 1993 PCR prize may reduce perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allows site-specific incorporation of non-natural amino acids in living cells and organisms, creating a new chemistry for proteins. The principle is clear and the capabilities, from protein probes to engineered biologics, are broad and generative.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues established the first orthogonal pairs and many amino acid incorporations; Chin extended the code to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet and orthogonal ribosome systems; Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama had decisive contributions, so selecting only two names involves a real judgment about priority.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of independent confirmation, with clinical-stage use of unnatural-amino-acid proteins. The field is mature, though it overlaps the 2018 evolution and 2024 protein-design prizes in spirit.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is not clear.
Whether the practical impact beyond research tools has yet reached the level expected for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase so the stoichiometry, composition and dynamics of intact protein complexes and membrane proteins can be measured. This is a quantitative physical-chemical capability that gave new access to molecular machines, and it complements structural biology methods that have been recognised.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck led the development and expansion to large complexes and membrane proteins, while Loo and Gross contributed foundational ESI work on non-covalent complexes. Three names are plausible but the early priority record is complicated, and ESI itself was recognised in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently adopted across structural biology, with ongoing growth into membrane proteins and native-like analysis; timing is reasonable though the method is seen as enabling more than discovery-driven.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers it an extension of the 2002 electrospray prize.
Claims of gas-phase structure preservation are accepted but remain subject to some debate.
Credit order among Robinson, Heck, Chait, Loo and Gross.
